page: Amazon Web Services r9g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton ARMv9 architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs utilizing the ARM Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. Each core has access to 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, supported by a 48 MB shared L3 cache. Memory configuration totals 128.0 GB of RAM, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, and features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread execution and exceptional memory subsystem responsiveness. Geekbench single-core reaches 2433.0 points alongside top-tier text processing and top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.23 GB/sec. PassMark memory testing registers a top-tier score of 4629.83, matching high memory bandwidth measured at 183.0 GB/sec for large read blocks and 74.02 GB/sec for large write blocks. Multithreaded scaling is solid, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 20291.0, while PassMark database operations and multi-threaded compression metrics place firmly within the upper tier. However, sustained compute benchmarks such as stress-ng and CPU encryption sit in the average performance tier.

Qualitatively, the Neoverse-V3 architecture delivers elevated memory throughput and single-core efficiency without the overhead of simultaneous multithreading, ensuring predictable per-core performance. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of integrated local NVMe storage and lack of GPU hardware acceleration, which makes the instance poorly suited for heavy local I/O buffering or large-scale AI model prompt processing. The r9g.4xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput static web serving, real-time analytics, and medium-scale ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.4xlarge is an ARM-based memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated Neoverse-V3 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, 128.0 GB of system memory, and Nitro hypervisor virtualization. Offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system achieves top-tier results in single-core Geekbench performance, memory benchmark suites, and text processing, supported by an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance omits bundled local SSD storage, depending entirely on remote EBS volumes, and contains no hardware accelerators. While stress-ng execution and large-parameter language model processing remain at average or baseline levels, the combination of dedicated cores and high memory bandwidth makes the r9g.4xlarge well suited for in-memory caching layers, Redis deployments, relational databases, static web delivery, and memory-constrained data manipulation.
